issues.description: The problem instructions explicitly tell students not to rename columns with AS unless requested (problem statement lines 101-103), but the reference solution for Aufgabe 01 aliases the name column to id (SELECT name as id, name, art, url ...). This causes a structural mismatch between the stated output (ID, Name, Art, URL) and the solution (which fabricates an ID by aliasing name), and may confuse students about whether they should use the real ID column or alias another column.
issues.suggestedFix: Adjust the reference solution to select the actual ID column (e.g. SELECT id, name, art, url FROM Schwimmbad WHERE art='Freibad') or update the problem instructions to explicitly allow aliasing for this task. Prefer selecting the real ID column to match the problem text and avoid aliasing.

issues.description: The problem statement asks for the columns 'ID, Name, Art und URL' for Freibäder, implying a distinct identifier column (ID). The solution, however, aliases the 'name' column as 'id' (SELECT name as id, name, art, url ...), effectively using the name as the ID. The template uses SELECT * FROM Schwimmbad, which does not make the expected identifier column explicit. This inconsistent use of 'ID' vs. 'name' as the identifier creates confusion for students about which column is the record identifier and which column is the display name.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier naming across artifacts. Either (A) make the schema and solution return the actual ID column (e.g. SELECT id, name, art, url FROM Schwimmbad WHERE art='Freibad') so 'ID' refers to the real identifier, or (B) change the problem text to request 'Name (als ID), Name, Art, URL' if intentionally using name as the ID. Prefer option A: use the real id column and avoid aliasing name to id.
